section: SC/ST rights - Articles 15, 16, 17, 46, 164, 244, 330, 332, 335; abolition of untouchability
subsections: Part XVI (Articles 330-342) - special provisions for certain classes
SC population data - India and AP (Census 2011)

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 335 — Claims of SCs and STs to services and posts
Article 340 — Lists of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes
Article 338B — Union control over Scheduled Areas
accepted.x: Article 335 concerns the claims of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes to services and posts. Article 339 concerns Union control over Scheduled Areas, Article 340 concerns backward classes, and Article 338B establishes the NCBC.
accepted.tq: Use the article–subject association and eliminate swapped constitutional bodies.
accepted.sec: Part XVI (Articles 330-342) - special provisions for certain classes  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Articles 338, 338A and 338B of the Constitution respectively relate to which of the following bodies?
accepted.x: Article 338 establishes the National Commission for Scheduled Castes, Article 338A the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes, and Article 338B the National Commission for Backward Classes.
accepted.tq: Recall the consecutive constitutional articles by matching each body with its exact provision.
accepted.sec: Part XVI (Articles 330-342) - special provisions for certain classes  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The provision relating to women's reservation in legislatures is associated with which one of the following constitutional provisions and amendments?
accepted.x: Article 334A was inserted in connection with women's reservation by the 106th Constitutional Amendment of 2023.
accepted.tq: Separate the provisions for existing SC/ST reservation from the newer provision for women's reservation.
accepted.sec: Part XVI (Articles 330-342) - special provisions for certain classes  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the constitutional provisions concerning the lists of certain classes?
o: Articles 341 and 342 concern SC and ST lists, while Article 342A concerns SEBC lists
Articles 338 and 338A concern SC and ST lists, while Article 342 concerns SEBC lists
Articles 339 and 340 concern SC and ST lists, while Article 341 concerns SEBC lists
Articles 330 and 332 concern SC and ST lists, while Article 342A concerns Anglo-Indian lists
accepted.x: Article 341 concerns the list of Scheduled Castes, Article 342 the list of Scheduled Tribes, and Article 342A concerns socially and educationally backward classes.
accepted.tq: Compare the neighbouring list-related articles and reject the commission and reservation provisions.
accepted.sec: Part XVI (Articles 330-342) - special provisions for certain classes  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: After the 2008 delimitation based on Census 2001, the number of seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha was respectively:
accepted.x: After the 2008 delimitation based on Census 2001, 84 Lok Sabha seats were reserved for SCs and 47 for STs. The earlier figures based on the 1971 population were 79 and 41 respectively.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the current post-delimitation figures from the earlier 1971-base figures.
accepted.sec: Part XVI (Articles 330-342) - special provisions for certain classes  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Lok Sabha seats reserved for SCs and STs:
1. The post-2008 figures were based on Census 2001.
2. The number of SC-reserved seats increased from the 1971-base figure.
3. The number of ST-reserved seats increased from 41 to 47.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The post-2008 delimitation used Census 2001, and the reserved seats rose from 79 to 84 for SCs and from 41 to 47 for STs.
accepted.tq: Check the base year and compare both pairs of numerical figures.
accepted.sec: Part XVI (Articles 330-342) - special provisions for certain classes  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: According to Census 2011 data, the Scheduled Castes constituted approximately what proportion of India's population?
accepted.x: Scheduled Castes constituted 16.6% of India's population according to Census 2011 data. The figure of 20.14 crore represents the SC population in absolute terms, not the percentage.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the percentage figure from the corresponding absolute population figure.
accepted.sec: SC population data - India and AP (Census 2011)  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Scheduled Caste population of India according to Census 2011 was approximately:
accepted.x: The Scheduled Caste population of India was 20.14 crore, or 201.4 million, according to Census 2011 data.
accepted.tq: Convert between crore and million figures without confusing the national and Andhra Pradesh data.
accepted.sec: SC population data - India and AP (Census 2011)  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Scheduled Caste population data in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: The SC population was 64.47 lakh and constituted 17.08% of the population.
The SC population was 84.69 lakh and constituted 24.85% of the population.
The SC population was 84.69 lakh and constituted 17.08% of the population.
The SC population was 20.14 crore and constituted 16.6% of the population.
accepted.x: In Andhra Pradesh, the SC population was 84.69 lakh and constituted 17.08% of the population. The other figures refer to India, a district share, or SC literacy.
accepted.tq: Separate absolute population, population share and literacy figures.
accepted.sec: SC population data - India and AP (Census 2011)  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which district recorded the highest Scheduled Caste population share in Andhra Pradesh, according to the data given?
accepted.x: Dr B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema recorded the highest SC population share at 24.85%. Alluri Sitharama Raju recorded the lowest share at 2.49%.
accepted.tq: Compare the extreme values rather than selecting the district associated with current administrative review.
accepted.sec: SC population data - India and AP (Census 2011)  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Scheduled Caste literacy rate in Andhra Pradesh referred to in the data is:
accepted.x: The Scheduled Caste literacy rate in Andhra Pradesh is given as 64.47%. The other percentages represent population shares or distractor values.
accepted.tq: Identify the literacy percentage instead of confusing it with district or state population shares.
accepted.sec: SC population data - India and AP (Census 2011)  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following districts had the lowest Scheduled Caste population share in Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: Alluri Sitharama Raju had the lowest Scheduled Caste population share at 2.49%, whereas Dr B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema had the highest at 24.85%.
accepted.tq: Use the lowest–highest contrast to identify the correct district and percentage.
accepted.sec: SC population data - India and AP (Census 2011)  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs of Andhra Pradesh Lok Sabha constituencies is correctly identified as reserved for Scheduled Castes?
accepted.x: Amalapuram, Bapatla, Chittoor and Tirupati are the four Andhra Pradesh Lok Sabha constituencies identified as reserved for Scheduled Castes.
accepted.tq: Recall the complete state-specific list and select a pair wholly drawn from it.

accepted.s:
Which one of the following is the correct chronological order of the following events?
A. Siddhantam temple entry
B. Karamchedu incident
C. Tsundur incident
D. Davinder Singh judgment
accepted.x: The Siddhantam temple entry took place in 1933, Karamchedu in 1985, Tsundur in 1991, and the Davinder Singh judgment in 2024.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the two intermediate incidents by year.

accepted.s: The Madiga Dandora movement and the Andhra Pradesh Act of 2000 are associated with which constitutional and legal debate?
o: Reservation of women in local bodies
Recognition of Scheduled Tribes in the Fifth Schedule
accepted.x: The Madiga Dandora movement and the 2000 Andhra Pradesh Act initiated the sub-classification debate within the Scheduled Castes, which culminated in the Davinder Singh judgment of 2024.
accepted.tq: Link the regional movement and legislation to the specific reservation debate they generated.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about constitutional reservation provisions is correct?
o: Article 16(4) formed part of the original Constitution, whereas Article 15(4) was added by the First Amendment in 1951.
Article 15(4) formed part of the original Constitution, whereas Article 16(4) was added by the First Amendment in 1951.
Both Articles 15(4) and 16(4) were inserted by the 42nd Amendment.
Both Articles 15(4) and 16(4) were inserted by the 1st Amendment.
accepted.x: Article 16(4) was present in the original Constitution. Article 15(4) was the first reservation clause added by constitutional amendment, through the First Amendment Act, 1951.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the original provision and the later amendment-created provision.

accepted.s: The Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955 is significant because it was:
o: The first law providing reservation in the Lok Sabha
The first law using the expression Scheduled Tribes
The first law creating the National Commission for Scheduled Castes
accepted.x: The Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955 was the first law enacted to enforce Article 17. The Government of India Act, 1935 had earlier used the term Scheduled Castes.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the first enforcement law from the earlier statutory use of the term Scheduled Castes.

accepted.s: The poem *Gabbilam*, associated with sensitising public opinion against untouchability, was composed by:
accepted.x: *Gabbilam* was composed by Gurram Jashuva and is associated with creating awareness against untouchability.
accepted.tq: Match the literary work with its author using the Andhra social-reform context.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Karamchedu occurred in 1985. Tsundur occurred in 1991, the Siddhantam temple entry was in 1933, and the Davinder Singh judgment was in 2024.
accepted.tq: Use the year–event pairing and reject the deliberately shifted dates.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the status of converts in relation to Scheduled Caste recognition is correct?
o: The judgment concerned only the nomination of Anglo-Indians to the Lok Sabha.
The judgment abolished all reservation for Scheduled Castes in Andhra Pradesh.
The Supreme Court in Chinthada Anand v. State of Andhra Pradesh held that Christian converts cannot claim Scheduled Caste status.
The Supreme Court held that every religious convert automatically retains Scheduled Caste status.
accepted.x: In Chinthada Anand v. State of Andhra Pradesh, the Supreme Court held that Christian converts cannot claim Scheduled Caste status. The case did not concern Anglo-Indian nomination or abolition of reservations.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise holding instead of accepting broad or absolute claims about conversion and reservation.

accepted.s: The K.G. Balakrishnan Commission concerning the Scheduled Caste status of Dalit Christians and Muslims was extended up to:
accepted.x: The tenure of the K.G. Balakrishnan Commission was extended up to 10 June 2026.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the exact extension date from nearby years.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements best reflects the criticism concerning the constitutional treatment of untouchability?
o: Because Article 17 is a directive principle, it cannot support penal legislation.
Because Article 17 applies only to public employment, private discrimination is fully excluded from debate.
Because Article 17 defines every possible form exhaustively, no new form can escape penalty.
Because untouchability is left undefined, new indirect forms may escape penal consequences.
accepted.x: A major criticism is that untouchability is not constitutionally defined, allowing newer indirect forms to potentially escape effective penal consequences.
accepted.tq: Apply the legal criticism to a situation involving newer indirect forms rather than relying on an absolute statement.

accepted.s: Which statement correctly describes the Centre's position on an income-based creamy layer in SC/ST reservations in August 2026?
o: It transferred the decision exclusively to State SC Commissions.
It opposed an income-based creamy layer and stated that any change requires a holistic empirical review.
It declared that creamy-layer rules already apply identically to all SC and ST quotas.
It supported immediate introduction of an income-based creamy layer without further study.
accepted.x: The Centre's affidavit opposed an income-based creamy layer in SC/ST quotas and stated that any change would require a holistic empirical review.
accepted.tq: Identify the authority's stated position and reject the extreme alternatives of immediate or automatic application.

accepted.s:
The 131st Constitutional Amendment Bill referred to in April 2026 sought to:
1. Amend Articles 330, 332 and 334A.
2. Enlarge the Lok Sabha to 850 members.
3. Create separate State Commissions for Scheduled Castes through Article 338(9).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
accepted.x: The Bill sought to amend Articles 330, 332 and 334A and enlarge the Lok Sabha to 850 members. It did not create State SC Commissions through Article 338(9), and the Bill had not been passed.
accepted.tq: Reject the statement that assigns a State-law function to the wrong constitutional provision.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the recent Andhra Pradesh-related developments?
o: K.S. Jawahar — review of SC/ST schemes in SPSR Nellore
B.V. Nagarathna — Chairman of the State SC Commission in Nellore
K.G. Balakrishnan — organiser of the Madiga Dandora movement
accepted.x: K.S. Jawahar, Chairman of the State SC Commission, reviewed SC/ST schemes in SPSR Nellore. B.V. Nagarathna is a Supreme Court judge, Chinthada Anand is a case name, and K.G. Balakrishnan headed the commission on the status of converts.
accepted.tq: Match the person with the correct institutional or legal role and reject swapped identities.

accepted.s: In the Sabarimala reference, Justice B.V. Nagarathna observed that Article 17 cannot be applied:
o: After the commencement of the Constitution
Only during the annual pilgrimage season
accepted.x: Justice B.V. Nagarathna stated that Article 17 cannot apply “for three days a month” in the Sabarimala reference.
accepted.tq: Recall the precise time-related phrase rather than replacing it with a broader limitation.

accepted.s: The petition by 32 Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe Congress MPs concerning the Haldwani “shuddhikaran” row was submitted to the:
accepted.x: The 32 SC/ST Congress MPs petitioned the President of India concerning the Haldwani “shuddhikaran” row.
accepted.tq: Identify the constitutional authority approached in the reported development.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements correctly reflects the recent action of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes?
o: It amended Article 338 through executive order after an alleged remark by a Chief Minister.
It dissolved the State SC Commission of Andhra Pradesh under Article 338(9).
It took suo motu cognisance of an alleged remark by a Chief Minister under Article 338.
It transferred all complaints to the NCBC under Article 342A.
accepted.x: The NCSC took suo motu cognisance of an alleged remark by a Chief Minister under Article 338. It cannot amend the Constitution or dissolve a State commission through the powers described.
accepted.tq: Match the constitutional body with its investigative action while rejecting powers assigned to the wrong authority.
